$about: Sprint-0 Gate 11. Every number here was MEASURED, never chosen from a document.
Errata E6 (rank 1) struck the approved 250 KB bundle number because it and the
approved 2.0 s TTI are mutually unsatisfiable, and ruled: register the ratchet
NAME with direction monotonic_down and NO VALUE ROW until the gate measures.
Until this file existed the null-budget build failure E6 calls 'the only gate
before then' did not exist anywhere in the tree — the build was green because
nothing measured, not because anything passed.
Direction is monotonic_down on every row: a number here may be TIGHTENED freely
and LOOSENED only deliberately. The engine half of that (ref.ci_ratchet, 05c
10.0.1) EXISTS since migration 0022 and check-perf-budgets.ts compares the two,
failing with PERF006 when the file and the engine ship different numbers. This
paragraph used to end 'is NOT built yet, so today loosening a value is still a
file edit' — it was true when written and had stopped being true, which is the
specific way a file like this goes quietly wrong.
What is still a file edit is a run that cannot REACH the engine: CI needs crm_ci
with LOGIN and a password set out of band. Such a run prints a box saying the
cross-check did not happen rather than passing in silence.
Every row now names a tier, and every tier names the command that runs it. A
tier nothing runs fails with PERF007 — P20 sat in an imaginary 'nightly' tier
for a month and looked, from this file, exactly like a budget being enforced.

budgets.name: perf.P12_initial_js_gzip
budgets.title: Initial JS, pipeline route
note: Measured from the client module graph, then cross-checked against a real
browser on both Playwright profiles: 105.6 KB gzip over 10 files, identical
to the byte. The graph computation is what runs here — it needs no browser,
no database and no session, and /board redirects when signed out.
Headroom is ~18% over the measurement, deliberately not zero. This budget
exists to catch a REGRESSION — the shape of it being the 147 KB gzip
better-auth 'identity' chunk reaching a seller-facing route — not to fail
the build the next time a screen gains a component.

budgets.name: perf.P13_initial_css_gzip
budgets.title: Initial CSS, pipeline route
note: 2.3 KB today for the whole design system, so the headroom looks large in
relative terms and is not. Three of the thirteen modules have any UI at all;
the token layers and the screens still to come land here.

budgets.name: perf.P6_drag_frames
budgets.title: Drag at 60 fps, 500-card board
note: 04b 3.2 P6: rAF deltas during a scripted 1200 ms three-column drag on a
500-card board. Fails on p95 > 20 ms, OR any frame > 34 ms, OR any long
task > 50 ms. Three separate failures, not one — a smooth average with a
single 60 ms stall is a drag that visibly jumps.
Enforced by tests/e2e/drag-perf.spec.ts, not by check-perf-budgets.ts:
this one needs a browser and a seeded board. The numbers live here so
there is one place they can be read from and one place they can be
loosened from.
The profile is dnd-ci — desktop-ci with a 2x CPU slowdown (04b 3.1), so a
green build means headroom on a seller's five-year-old laptop rather than
60 fps on a CI runner with nothing else to do.

budgets.name: perf.P20_mobile_tti_pipeline
budgets.title: Mobile time-to-interactive, /pipeline
note: GATE 11 IS CLOSED. Measured by tests/e2e/tti.spec.ts under the lh-ci profile,
against the PRODUCTION build on :3001 and the perf-500 fixture (500 cards,
6 stages), signed in as the fixture seller. Lighthouse's own mobile preset,
unmodified: 4x CPU slowdown, simulated slow 4G, phone viewport.
Five runs measured 2227 2248 2251 2265 2276 ms — a spread of 49 ms. Per 8.1
the median rounded up to the next 100 ms becomes the budget: 2251 -> 2300,
inside the 3000 ms ceiling. The gate compares the MEDIAN of 3 runs, never
the best of them and never the mean.
FCP and TTI land on the same millisecond, and that is a real property of
this architecture rather than a broken measurement: the board is server
rendered, so the pixels exist at first paint, and React hydrates 500 cards
in interruptible chunks that never produce a task over 50 ms. Total blocking
time is 2-10 ms. If either of those stops being true, TTI leaves FCP behind
and this budget is what notices.
MACHINE-DEPENDENT, unlike P12 and P13. Those count bytes; this multiplies
observed task durations by four, so a slower runner measures a larger TTI.
Re-baselining onto different hardware is a deliberate act: the row is
monotonic_down and ref.ci_ratchet refuses a loosening with AP002.
The nightly tier this row used to name was abandoned rather than built.
Scheduled Actions minutes cost money and 9.4.1 makes the absence of a
payment method the cost control, so a nightly job is a gate that gets
switched off. The e2e suite already serves this exact build for Gate 12.

budgets.name: perf.N13_search_server_p95
budgets.title: Global search, server p95
note: P5.3 N13. The SERVER p95 is the budget; US-LCP-08's 500 ms end-to-end is
'a consequence, not a budget' and is deliberately not ratcheted here.
MEASURED at 55-60 ms across 25,000 contacts in 50 books, over the six
queries §7 puts a seller in front of: a pasted number, a number typed
with hyphens, the last four digits, a surname with many matches, a first
name with more, and an email fragment.
120, not 60. The budget exists to catch a REGRESSION, not to break the
build the next time a result row gains a column — the same deliberate
headroom P12 was given over its own measurement, for the same reason.
The first measurement was 1,053 ms. Nothing about the schema changed to
fix it: migration 0011 already had the composite GIN over
(tenant_id, owner_user_id, full_name gin_trgm_ops), and the query was
written so it could not be used. Scoping in a CTE and matching in a
LATERAL forced a sequential scan of the tenant on every keystroke.
Enforced by tests/integration/search-perf.test.ts, not by
check-perf-budgets.ts: this one needs a database and a 25,000-contact
fixture. The number lives here so there is one place to read it from and
one place it can be loosened from.
